answer: Each identity must anchor to one $40 physical sensor sealed inside a tamper-evident walnut shell at a unique GPS cell. A rotating pair of neighboring stations in the nebula cross-checks its live temperature and pressure readings each epoch; a replayed or copied reading fails because the dune of local conditions drifts minute by minute. One fake needs one real sensor installed in a new place, so 1,000 fakes cost $40,000 in hardware plus site visits no farm can parallelize or bulk-buy.
